chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) bequeathed to al-Ḥasan, and he made al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام), Muḥammad, all of his children, the chiefs of his Shiʿah, and the people of his household witnesses to his bequest. Then he handed over to him the Book and the weapon.

Then he said to his son al-Ḥasan: “O my son, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم commanded me to bequeath to you, and to hand over to you my books and my weapon, just as the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم bequeathed to me and handed over to me his books and his weapon. And he commanded me to command you that, when death comes to you, you should hand it over to your brother al-Ḥusayn.”

Then he turned to his son al-Ḥusayn and said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم commanded you to hand it over to this son of yours,” then he took the hand of his grandson ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn.

Then he said to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn: “O my son, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم commanded you to hand it over to your son Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, and convey to him greetings from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and from me.”

Then he turned to his son al-Ḥasan and said: “O my son, you are the holder of the authority and the guardian of the blood. So if you pardon, that is for you; and if you kill, then one strike in place of one strike, and you do not sin.”

key_terms.السِّلَاحَ: the weapon, entrusted as part of the legacy of authority
key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: the Book, meaning the transmitted scripture or written corpus entrusted as a sign of authority
key_terms.ضَرْبَةٌ مَكَانَ ضَرْبَةٍ: one strike in place of one strike, indicating equal retaliation
key_terms.وَلِيُّ الدَّمِ: the one entitled to decide regarding retaliation for blood
key_terms.وَلِيُّ الْأَمْرِ: the one vested with authority over the affair

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the transfer of authority and trust from Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) to the later Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the bequest of Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) to al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام), including the transfer of the books and weapon as signs of divinely designated authority. It also describes the succession through al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام), ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, and Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, while concluding with guidance regarding authority over retaliation and pardon.
